empires.name: The Kingdom of Kush
empires.note: The Land of the Bow - archers who outrange anything Egypt fields, and iron from the Meroe furnaces in every spearhead. Six cataracts bar the river above Aswan, so a fleet coming south drags its hulls over bare rock while the bowmen wait on the cliffs.

places.name: Meroe
places.note: The throne. Slag heaps from the iron furnaces ring the city, and the royal pyramids stand on the ridge above.

places.name: Napata
places.note: The old seat under Jebel Barkal, holy mountain of Amun - the priests here still name kings.

places.name: Kerma
places.note: Mud-brick walls thicker than a house is wide, guarding the grain of the Dongola reach.

places.name: Kawa
places.note: Temple town and horse country; Kushite cavalry mounts are bred on this stretch of river.

places.name: Naqa
places.note: Out in the Butana grass, watered by cisterns - cut them and the town dies in a month.

places.name: Musawwarat es-Sufra
places.note: A walled enclosure of courts and ramps where the war elephants are kept and trained.

places.name: Qasr Ibrim
places.note: A crag fort over the river in Lower Nubia; nothing sails past it unseen or untaxed.

places.name: Buhen
places.note: Old Egyptian fortress at the Second Cataract, now held by Kushite bowmen against the north.

places.name: Pnubs
places.note: Palm groves and a small temple on Argo island - a granary with no wall around it.

empires.name: The Inca Empire
empires.note: Rope bridges and paved roads cross every gorge and ridge - their columns march where yours cannot climb. Runners with knotted cords carry word the length of the empire in days, so no advance of yours is a surprise, and the hillside storehouses never run empty.

places.name: Cusco
places.note: The throne, laid out as a puma between two rivers. Fitted stone walls, no mortar, and a fortress on the hill above.

places.name: Quito
places.note: The northern seat, a second court on the equator - the road from Cusco ends at its gate.

places.name: Cajamarca
places.note: Hot springs, a great walled plaza, and the army of the north quartered around it.

places.name: Tumbes
places.note: The empire's port on the warm sea, where balsa rafts come in with shell and gold.

places.name: Ollantaytambo
places.note: Terraces climbing to a stone gate that closes the Urubamba valley to anything marching upriver.

places.name: Tiwanaku
places.note: Ruins of the older people by Lake Titicaca; the herds on the high plain here feed the whole south.

places.name: Huanuco Pampa
places.note: A road-station city of five hundred storehouses on the ridge - take it and an army starves.

places.name: Pachacamac
places.note: Oracle on the coast that predates the empire; pilgrims and their offerings pass through unarmed.

places.name: Machu Picchu
places.note: A royal estate on a saddle above the gorge, reached by one path wide enough for one man.
